# Florence 1490 – Mathematics & measurement

- **Zero and positional notation** [`zero_place_value`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/zero_place_value.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Roman numerals survive for dates, inscriptions and some formal totals, thought harder to falsify.
- **Hindu-Arabic numerals and written arithmetic** [`arabic_numerals`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/arabic_numerals.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Taught in abacus schools for merchants' sons. Fibonacci was from Pisa. Local: abacus schools; Filippo Calandri.
- **Abacus and counting board** [`abacus_counting_board`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/abacus_counting_board.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept low. In Italy 'abbaco' now means pen reckoning with numerals; counters on a lined board are northern and old-fashioned. A bead frame is unknown. Elsewhere: Germany and France (reckoning counters); China (suanpan).
- **Common fractions and the rule of three** [`fractions_rule_of_three`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fractions_rule_of_three.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. The daily bread of commerce: exchange, alloying, partnership shares are all solved by the rule of three. Local: abacus schools; Filippo Calandri.
- **Decimal fractions** [`decimal_fractions`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/decimal_fractions.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept high. Florentine merchants favour common fractions and mixed units. Astronomers usually use sixtieths, but Bianchini used decimal fractions in fifteenth-century Ferrara. Elsewhere: Ferrara, Giovanni Bianchini's astronomical tables; Samarkand, al-Kashi's decimal fractions.
- **Negative numbers** [`negative_numbers`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/negative_numbers.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. A negative answer is read as a debt or thrown out as absurd. Ledgers avoid them with separate debit and credit sides. Elsewhere: Lyon, Nicolas Chuquet's manuscript (1484); India and China.
- **Square roots and irrational numbers** [`square_roots_irrationals`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/square_roots_irrationals.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Abacus masters extract roots by hand and call the inexact ones deaf (radici sorde). Whether these are numbers at all is doubted.
- **Logarithms** [`logarithms`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/logarithms.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Tables must be computed by hand: months of work for a team of abacus masters. Astrologers and astronomers gain most; needs decimal fractions first. Local: abacus masters.
- **Slide rule** [`slide_rule`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/slide_rule.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Needs a logarithm table first, then an instrument maker to engrave the scales on boxwood or brass. Local: makers of astrolabes and quadrants.
- **Symbolic algebra** [`symbolic_algebra`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/symbolic_algebra.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Abacus writers use names and abbreviations for unknowns and powers. Several local manuscripts handle more than one unknown. Notation varies from author to author. Local: Florentine abacus masters and their manuscripts. Elsewhere: Leipzig, Widmann prints + and - (1489).
- **Solving quadratic and cubic equations** [`quadratic_cubic_equations`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/quadratic_cubic_equations.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Abacus masters teach quadratic cases, and special cubics admit solutions. A general method for the cubic is still missing. Local: Florentine abacus masters; Piero della Francesca (Sansepolcro). Elsewhere: university of Bologna.
- **Systems of linear equations (elimination and matrices)** [`linear_equations_matrices`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/linear_equations_matrices.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Abacus texts use false position and sometimes several unknowns. A systematic array of coefficients would offer a general procedure for simultaneous equations. Elsewhere: China, fangcheng array method.
- **Complex numbers** [`complex_numbers`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/complex_numbers.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Even negative roots are suspect; a root of a negative is an impossible case. No use until the cubic is solved.
- **Prime numbers and number theory** [`prime_numbers_number_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/prime_numbers_number_theory.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. Euclid's books on numbers and Boethius are studied; perfect and amicable numbers attract Neoplatonists for their meaning, not their use.
- **Combinatorics (permutations, combinations, Pascal's triangle)** [`combinatorics_permutations`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/combinatorics_permutations.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Dice players know the throws are not equally common. Counting arrangements appears as puzzles; Llull's combining art is known to Pico.
- **Compound interest and exponential growth** [`compound_interest_exponential_growth`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/compound_interest_exponential_growth.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept medium. Bankers compound yearly (fare capo d'anno). Open interest is usury, so it hides in exchange rates and 'gifts' on deposits. Local: Medici bank; Monte delle Doti (state dowry fund); abacus schools.
- **Deductive geometry and proof (Euclid, Pythagoras)** [`geometry_proof`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/geometry_proof.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Euclid is in print in Latin (Venice 1482). Universities read the first books; craftsmen learn recipes for areas and volumes without proof. Local: Piero della Francesca (Sansepolcro); abacus schools; university of Pisa.
- **Pi and the measurement of the circle** [`pi_circle_measurement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pi_circle_measurement.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept medium. Craftsmen use 22/7 and many take it for exact. Squaring the circle is still thought possible. Elsewhere: Samarkand, al-Kashi's 16 decimals (1424); Kerala, Madhava's series.
- **Trigonometry** [`trigonometry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/trigonometry.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Sine tables serve astronomers and astrologers only. Regiomontanus' book on triangles is still unprinted; surveyors and gunners use shadow squares and similar triangles. Elsewhere: Nuremberg (Regiomontanus' papers), Augsburg (his Tabulae directionum with tangent table, printed 1490).
- **Coordinate geometry and graphs of functions** [`coordinate_geometry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coordinate_geometry.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Ptolemy's maps use a grid of latitude and longitude; painters copy through squared veils; Oresme's latitude of forms is in print. No one links curves to equations. Local: Berlinghieri's printed Ptolemy (Florence 1482); painters' workshops.
- **Non-Euclidean geometry** [`non_euclidean_geometry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/non_euclidean_geometry.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low
- **Linear perspective and technical drawing** [`perspective_technical_drawing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/perspective_technical_drawing.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Florence invented painters' perspective. Machines are built from wooden models and sketchbook views, not from measured plan-and-elevation drawings. Local: painters' workshops (Ghirlandaio; Botticelli); Giuliano da Sangallo; Piero della Francesca (Sansepolcro).
- **Surveying, levelling and triangulation** [`surveying_triangulation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/surveying_triangulation.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept high. Land is measured with rods and cords, levels taken with a plumb-line frame; Alberti described surveying by bearings. No triangulated maps exist. Local: catasto (tax survey) officials; river and fortification engineers.
- **Solar calendar with leap years** [`solar_calendar_leap_years`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/solar_calendar_leap_years.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The spring equinox falls roughly nine days before its conventional date of 21 March. Florence numbers the new year from 25 March. Calendar reform requires agreement. Local: Toscanelli's gnomon in the Duomo.
- **Decimal, coherent system of units (metric system)** [`metric_system_units`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/metric_system_units.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Every city has its own braccio, libbra and staio, and guards them as a sign of sovereignty. Merchants live with conversion handbooks.
- **Probability and statistics** [`probability_statistics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/probability_statistics.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Dice, insurance contracts, grain accounts and burial registers supply examples. Merchants already distinguish risk by route, though they lack a formal calculus of probability. Local: Grain Office and burial registers; marine insurers; dice players. Elsewhere: Milan, civic death registers.

- **Errors of measurement, the bell curve and least squares** [`normal_distribution_errors`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/normal_distribution_errors.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Astronomers compare observations and revise tables. Repeated readings of one angle offer a way to introduce a distribution of errors.
- **Graphs of data (line, bar and pie charts)** [`data_graphs`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/data_graphs.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Prices, deaths and exchange rates are kept as lists and tables. Drawing them as a line over time is new and needs only paper.
